answer: A bridge operator can require each agent to lock a small refundable deposit before crossing into the shared economy, so spawning thousands of fake identities stops being free. The deposit returns only after the agent completes real, verifiable work, and any identity caught cheating forfeits its stake to a public slashing pool. Like water slowly carving karst caves, the cost shapes honest behavior over time. One crystal rule governs all: stake first, earn trust through work, lose the stake if you lie — sybil farming turns unprofitable while honest agents keep working at near-zero cost.
